subject: Hosted API Capacity Increase — Incremental Commit & Billing Cadence
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@orchard.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API Capacity Increase — Incremental Commit & Billing Cadence

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. Per our discussion I put together a concise proposal for the hosted-API commit increase Orchard asked us to price out. High level:

- Current monthly committed tokens: 1,000,000 tokens
- Proposed monthly committed tokens: 2,500,000 tokens (2.5x)
- Proposed committed unit price: $0.0011 / token (blended across generation & embeddings tiers)
- Burst pocket: 600,000 tokens per month at 1.6x committed rate (available on-demand)
- Term: 12 months (auto-renew unless either party gives 60 days notice)
- Billing cadence: preference shown below (monthly invoicing, option to switch to quarterly with 1% discount)

Attached: 2027-05-12_Commit_Uplift_Proposal.pdf and Orchard_SOW_v3.xlsx with the operational handoff and runway plan for traffic ramp.

Two quick asks so we can finalize:
1) Can you confirm the requested effective date for the uplift (we penciled in 2027-06-01)?
2) Who in your procurement/AP should we invoice and what billing cadence will you need (monthly, quarterly, or net-45)?

Operational notes: we will provision a dedicated burst pool and pre-seed KV cache warmers ahead of your expected traffic spike; estimated latency impact is a 5-10ms median improvement for short-seq generation once warmed.

Looping Priya on billing cadence and Marissa for contract redlines. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk the SOW.

Best,

Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri**@redwood.ai
Attachments: 2027-05-12_Commit_Uplift_Proposal.pdf, Orchard_SOW_v3.xlsx
From: Alex Mercer <alex@orchard.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@orchard.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API Capacity Increase — Incremental Commit & Billing Cadence

Priyom,

Thanks for the clear proposal — this looks in the ballpark. A few clarifying points from our side before we take this to procurement: 

- Concurrency / rate-control: we need an explicit per-tenant rate limit (tokens/min) during burst events. Can you confirm the suggested per-minute cap for the dedicated burst pool?
- Pricing ceiling: as we're committing to 12 months, can Redwood guarantee the committed unit price (0.0011) will not increase during the term?
- Billing cadence: Orchard prefers net-45 for AP timing. If monthly invoices are the default, we need to confirm Redwood will accept net-45 on an annual commit and whether there's any fee for that.

If we can get answers on the above we can issue a PO. Also want to flag that security wants a short note on data isolation for the burst pool (we reviewed the SOW but please add a one-paragraph summary that we can attach to our internal security ticket).

Thanks — cc'ing Natalie (procurement) to keep them in the loop.

—Alex
CTO (acting), Orchard AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@orchard.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API Capacity Increase — Incremental Commit & Billing Cadence

Alex — thanks, good questions. Quick answers below and next steps: 

1) Rate limits / concurrency: for the dedicated burst pool we recommend a per-tenant soft cap of 1,500,000 tokens/min (burst throttled by continuous-batching layer) with a hard guard at 2,000,000 tokens/min. In practice the continuous batching will smooth peaks; we can instrument per-route throttles if you want stricter per-endpoint limits.

2) Price ceiling: Redwood will fix the committed unit price for the agreed 12-month term (no unit price increases within that term). If additional capacity is requested mid-term we will price on a pro-rata basis but will not raise the already-signed committed rate for existing commitment.

3) Billing cadence: we can accept net-45 for annual committed contracts. Standard practice is no fee for net-45 on annual commitments; for monthly-only contracts we normally require net-30. If you select quarterly invoicing we can offer a 1% billing discount (as noted).

4) Security note (summary to attach): Dedicated burst pool instances are logically isolated at the tenant layer; KV caches are per-tenant and encrypted at rest with customer-data keys. Audit logs for burst allocations and cache hits are available via the Console with configurable retention. We will add a 1-paragraph excerpt to the SOW and share as an appendix.

Next steps I propose: I will circulate a redline-ready Commitment Amendment (Marissa will prepare) and an updated invoice template. If Orchard confirms acceptance we can send the amendment via DocuSign and begin provisioning for the 2027-06-01 start.

Attached: updated proposal (minor clarifications).

Could Natalie confirm the AP contact and PO flow so Marissa and Priya can prepare the DocuSign + invoice?

Best,

Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: docusign_instructions.txt

- Effective date: 2027-06-01
- We will issue a PO to Redwood once we receive the DocuSign amendment. PO will reference DEAL-2027-0476.
- AP contact for invoicing: ap@orchard.ai (net-45)
- Signatory: Sarah Liao (VP Finance)

Please send the DocuSign link to Sarah and to ap@orchard.ai. Once the amendment is signed we'll trigger the PO in our system and schedule the provisioning window.

Thanks,
